title: Section counts for degree-one and general small effective divisors
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $C/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve [def-sc-curves, def-kun-projective] of genus $g\geq1$ [def-sc-genus]. Divisors and $\mathcal O_C(D)$ use [def-sc-divisor], and $h^0(C,\mathcal L):=\dim_kH^0(C,\mathcal L)$ uses [pqf-def-cohomology]. For every $Q\in C(k)$ one has $h^0(C,\mathcal O_C([Q]))=1$. For every integer $0\leq r\leq g$ there exists an effective divisor $D$ of degree $r$ on $C$ such that $h^0(C,\mathcal O_C(D))=1$. For $r=0$ one may take the zero divisor.

source.place: Chapter III proof of Proposition 2.3, pp.92–93 (no distinct linearly equivalent degree-one divisors in positive genus), and Lemma 5.2(a),(b), pp.101–102 (successively lowering h^1 and applying Riemann–Roch).

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper] the curve is proper. By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] it is Noetherian and integral, with DVRs at closed points and a generic point $\eta$; thus it is a regular curve. By [lem-sc-divisor-module-local], every $\mathcal O_C(D)$ is invertible and $\mathcal O_C(0)=\mathcal O_C$. Degrees in [def-sc-pic0] give $\deg\mathcal O_C(D)=\deg D$. Write $h^i(D)=\dim_kH^i(C,\mathcal O_C(D))$. Serre duality [thm-sc-serre-duality-curve] supplies finite dimensionality and vanishing above degree one. Riemann--Roch [lem-sc-riemann-roch] therefore reads $h^0(D)-h^1(D)=\deg D+1-g$. For $D=0$, the definition [def-sc-genus] gives $h^1(0)=g$, so $h^0(0)=1$. This already proves the $r=0$ assertion.

source.place: Chapter III, p.101, paragraph before Lemma 5.2 and its proof on p.102: Riemann--Roch, duality, and D_0=0; Stacks curves.tex Tags 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), 0BS6 (lemma-rr).

proof.text: Fix $Q\in C(k)$ and put $L=\mathcal O_C([Q])$. The rational function $1$ is a nonzero global section by [def-sc-divisor], so $h^0(L)\geq1$. If $g=1$, [def-sc-pic0] gives $\deg L=1=2g-1$ and [lem-sc-riemann-roch-large-degree] gives $h^0(L)=1+1-g=1$. If $g\geq2$, apply [lem-sfb-linear-series-degree-dimension-bound] to the nonzero finite-dimensional space $U=H^0(C,L)$, with $q=h^0(C,L)$ and $d=1$; [lem-pc-degree-agrees-sc] identifies its degree convention with this divisor degree. That node gives a number $0\leq a\leq1$ and $q\leq\max\{a+1-g,a/2+1\}\leq3/2$. As $q$ is a positive integer, $q=1$. This proves the degree-one clause for every $Q$, not just a general point.

source.place: Chapter III, proof of Proposition 2.3, pp.92--93: positive-genus degree-one assertion; agent reconstruction using the existing linear-series bound for g>=2 and the existing Riemann--Roch large-degree formula for g=1.

proof.text: Put $\omega=\Omega^1_{C/k}$, invertible by [lem-sc-canonical-sheaf]. For an effective divisor $D$, set $N_D=\omega\otimes\mathcal O_C(D)^{-1}$. The inverse is the dual by [lem-sc-invertible-dual]; tensor products use [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This is invertible: local generators of its two factors tensor to a generator. Locally at a closed point $P$, if $D$ has coefficient $n_P$ and $t$ is a uniformizer, [lem-sc-divisor-module-local] gives $\mathcal O_C(D)_P=t^{-n_P}\mathcal O_{C,P}$ and its inverse $t^{n_P}\mathcal O_{C,P}$. Increasing $n_Q$ by one therefore identifies $N_{D+[Q]}$ with the subsheaf of $N_D$ whose sections have value zero in the fibre $N_D(Q):=(N_D)_Q/\mathfrak m_Q(N_D)_Q$ at $Q$. Away from $Q$ the inclusion is the identity; at $Q$ its image is $t(N_D)_Q$. These local descriptions glue because each is the kernel of restriction to that fibre. Thus on global sections $H^0(C,N_{D+[Q]})$ is exactly the kernel of evaluation $H^0(C,N_D)\to N_D(Q)$.

source.place: Local divisor-module calculation used in Milne III Lemma 5.2(a), p.102; invertible modules locally free of rank one, and the local quotient by the maximal ideal. No cohomology exact-sequence theorem is being assumed.

proof.text: Suppose $h^1(D)>0$. By [thm-sc-serre-duality-curve], $h^0(C,N_D)=h^1(D)$, so choose a nonzero global section $s$ of $N_D$. By [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk], its generic germ is nonzero. Trivialize $N_D$ near $\eta$ and write $s=a e$; shrink this open to the nonvanishing locus of $a$. It is a nonempty open on which $s$ generates $N_D$. By [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] choose a $k$-rational point $Q$ in that open. Its fibre $N_D(Q)$ has dimension one over $k$, and $s(Q)\ne0$. Consequently evaluation onto that fibre is surjective. The kernel description of step 3 and finite-dimensional rank--nullity give $h^0(C,N_{D+[Q]})=h^0(C,N_D)-1$. Applying [thm-sc-serre-duality-curve] to $\mathcal O_C(D+[Q])$ now gives $h^1(D+[Q])=h^1(D)-1$. Notice that $Q$ is chosen after $D$; no uniform open in a parameter space is needed.

source.place: Chapter III, Lemma 5.2(a), pp.101--102: a nonzero section of the dual line bundle is nonvanishing on a nonempty open; evaluation there has rank one.

proof.text: For $0\leq j\leq g$ inductively construct an effective $D_j$ of degree $j$ with $h^1(D_j)=g-j$. Start with $D_0=0$, as in step 1. If $j<g$, then $g-j>0$ and step 4 supplies $Q_j\in C(k)$ with $h^1(D_j+[Q_j])=g-j-1$. Set $D_{j+1}=D_j+[Q_j]$; effectiveness and degree $j+1$ follow from the coefficient-sum definition [def-sc-divisor]. This establishes the induction, including $j=g$, where no further decrease is requested. For the prescribed integer $0\leq r\leq g$, choose $D=D_r$. The Riemann--Roch identity established in step 1 gives $h^0(D_r)=r+1-g+(g-r)=1$.

source.place: Chapter III, proof of Lemma 5.2(b), p.102: repeat (a) starting with D_0=0 and substitute h^1=g-r into Riemann--Roch.

proof_origin.place: Chapter III Proposition 2.3 and Lemma 5.2(a),(b), pp.92--93,101--102; the degree-one proof uses an existing Clifford/linear-series bound and the genus-one Riemann--Roch case; point selection and induction follow Milne.
